_comment: Every number that decides a score, declared in one place instead of scattered as literals
across three handler modules. These are the audit's methodology: what counts as a thin
page, where the keyword-stuffing line sits, how a share of clean pages maps to points.
They cannot be removed -- a scoring engine has to encode its scoring -- but they should be
readable, reviewable and changeable without editing a handler, which is what this file is
for. Anything here can be overridden per-deployment via SCORING_RULES_PATH.
Bands read best-first as [minimum value, points]. The first band whose threshold the
measured value meets wins; a value below every band gets `floor`.

question_headings._what: ON-01. Share of eligible headings phrased as a buyer question.
question_headings._why: Scoring the raw share meant full marks required ~90% of every H1-H3 to be a question, which no well-written page does, so the check could only ever FAIL. A third is the realistic target.

keyword_density._what: ON-09. Peak single-term density, measured over content words only.
keyword_density._why: With function words included the most frequent token on essentially every English page was 'the' at 4-7%, above the worst band, so every site scored the floor and the check said nothing.

cannibalization._what: ON-18. Share of the site NOT competing with itself for the same buyer question.
cannibalization._why: A fixed penalty per pair meant nine overlapping titles bottomed out the check whether the site had 20 pages or 2000. Proportional scales the penalty with the site.

dilution._what: ON-19. Share of the site that is neither thin nor near-duplicate.
dilution._why: Same reason as cannibalization: the old absolute penalty hit its cap at eight thin pages.

text_to_code._what: TECH-13. Visible text as a percentage of total HTML weight.

forum_mentions._what: OFF-07. Reddit, Quora and forum/community result pages found for the company name.
forum_mentions._why: A single thread is incidental; a handful across communities shows the company is genuinely discussed. The old 15/40/65 scale could never reach PASS, which misstated a well-discussed company as failing.

best_list_pages._what: OFF-08, when the company is not in the generic 'best <category>' results: list pages (best/top/leading in the title) that name it.
best_list_pages._why: Appearing on the generic results page is the strongest signal and scores 100 outright; being named on list pages found by name is the next tier.

thin_page_words._what: ON-19. Below this word count a page counts as thin.

near_duplicate_body_similarity._what: ON-19. Jaccard overlap of page text above which two pages are near-duplicates.

competing_title_similarity._what: ON-18. Jaccard overlap of titles above which two pages become candidates for competing. A candidate filter only -- the model confirms which genuinely compete.

min_content_words_for_density._what: ON-09, TECH-11. Below this, a page has too little prose for density or section-length to mean anything.

answer_direct_words._what: ON-02. An answer under a question heading must reach this length to count as a direct answer at all.

answer_ideal_words._what: ON-02. The registry's own 40-60 word target for a self-contained answer.

answer_acceptable_words._what: ON-02. Partial credit band around the ideal.

comparison_pages_for_full_credit._what: ON-17. How many genuine comparison pages a site needs before the check stops penalising it.

useful_list_min_items._what: ON-08. A list shorter than this is a fragment, not a procedure or criteria set.

redirect_chain_hops._what: TECH-06, TECH-20. At or above this many hops a redirect counts as a chain.

vitals_lcp_ms._what: TECH-07. Largest Contentful Paint, milliseconds (75th percentile for field data, median key page for lab). At or under `good` scores full marks; at or over `poor` scores the poor floor.
vitals_lcp_ms._why: Google's published Core Web Vitals thresholds (web.dev/articles/vitals).

vitals_inp_ms._what: TECH-07, field data only. Interaction to Next Paint, milliseconds, 75th percentile.
vitals_inp_ms._why: Google's published Core Web Vitals thresholds. INP needs real users interacting, so a lab run scores Total Blocking Time in its place.

vitals_tbt_ms._what: TECH-07, lab data only. Total Blocking Time, milliseconds: the lab stand-in for INP.
vitals_tbt_ms._why: Lighthouse's mobile scoring thresholds for TBT.

vitals_cls._what: TECH-07. Cumulative Layout Shift (unitless; largest session window).
vitals_cls._why: Google's published Core Web Vitals thresholds.

vitals_points._what: TECH-07. Points per metric: `good` at or under the good threshold; between the thresholds, falling linearly from `needs_improvement_best` to `needs_improvement_worst`; `poor` at or over the poor threshold. TECH-07 is the mean of the three metric scores.
vitals_points._why: Mirrors Google's three ratings (Good / Needs improvement / Poor) while still separating a site just over the line from one about to fail.

small_sample_items._what: TECH-19. Below this many items, a result is still reported but flagged as resting on very little evidence, with lower confidence.
small_sample_items._why: One valid JSON-LD block scored 100 and read as 'the site's markup is clean' when the site had almost no markup at all.

platforms_for_full_marks._what: OFF-03, OFF-05. Sites the company must be found on for full presence points (70). Presence = min(found, N) / N x 70, where N is this value or the number of sites checked, whichever is smaller.
platforms_for_full_marks._why: The site lists are configurable (offpage_platforms.json) and an industry or region adds sites to them. Dividing by the whole list would make a scan that checks more sites score lower for the same presence; dividing by a fixed N keeps the default four-site result unchanged and lets any of the checked sites count.

review_recent_days._what: OFF-06. A review-platform result dated within this many days earns the full recency points (40).
review_recent_days._why: Assistants and buyers discount reviews older than a year.

review_stale_days._what: OFF-06. A review-platform result dated within this many days (but not the recent window) earns half the recency points (20).
review_stale_days._why: Two-year-old reviews still show the company is reviewed, but no longer that it is currently active.

section_weights._what: Overall score. Share of the 100 points each section carries; must sum to 1.

redirect_chain_penalty._what: TECH-06. Points taken off per long redirect chain, and the most the chains can take off in total.

proxy_latency_ms._what: TECH-07 fallback when Core Web Vitals cannot be measured. Average response time in ms: at or under each limit scores its points; slower than every limit scores `floor`.

proxy_page_bytes._what: TECH-07 fallback. Average page weight in bytes: at or under each limit scores its points; heavier than every limit scores `floor`.

proxy_mix._what: TECH-07 fallback. How the latency and page-weight scores are blended.

impact_shares._what: Priority list. A finding is High Impact when the points it costs reach `high` x the mean parameter coefficient, Medium at `medium` x; fractions rather than fixed points so they follow the registry's weights.

working_tolerance._what: Score pop-up. The step-by-step working is shown only when its recomputed score is within this many points of the reported one.
